system:
You repair one knowledge atom that auditors sent back. Use only the supplied evidence sentences; add no background knowledge.

Rules for the repaired atoms:
- One independently assessable claim per atom, written as one sentence that is understood without the source.
- If the atom joined several claims, split it into separate atoms (at most 3), most important first.
- Every atom must be fully stated in the evidence sentences it cites. Remove anything the evidence does not state. Keep quantifiers, negation, hedges, and formulas (LaTeX in $...$).
- Remove procedural or evaluative add-ons and stacked conditions; keep a condition only if the claim is false without it.
- Drop attributions such as "the authors state" when the claim itself is general.
- Use the S label that fits: S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends.
- If no valid atom can be written from this evidence, return an empty list and explain in note.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"atoms": [{"statement": "...", "scope": "S1|S2|S3", "evidence_ids": ["..."]}], "note": ""}
user:
CONCEPT: allogeneic CAR-T cells

ATOM CART-C06-S2-01 (S2): Host-mediated rejection of allogeneic CAR-T cells can be addressed by disrupting CD52 so the cells resist an anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody, which suppresses all CD52+ immune cells, such as T, B, and NK cells, that can mediate rejection.

EVIDENCE:
[CART-p0057-s14] CAR-T cells have been genome edited to become resistant to an anti-CD52 monoclonal antibody through disruption of CD52 (Benjamin et al. 2020).
[CART-p0057-s15] This approach has the advantage of suppressing all CD52+ immune cells that can mediate rejection, such as T, B, and NK cells, although prolonged immunosuppression is associated with a higher risk of serious virus reactivation.

AUDITOR FINDINGS:
- GROUNDED: hold — The supplied sentences establish CD52 disruption and suppression of rejection-mediating cells, but do not state the allogeneic CAR-T population restriction.
- SINGLE_CLAIM: hold — Joins the engineering mechanism (disrupting CD52 to resist anti-CD52 antibody) with the immunological scope of the antibody (suppressing T, B, and NK cells).
